checks: Only the statement changed. The affine map first sends the simplex to the standard one; the subsequent translation sends its centroid to zero. The determinant bounds, the centered inradius and all angle estimates use this corrected common frame.

For any attaining cap with nonzero continuous normal at an interior y, replacing a lower threshold by the through-y threshold strictly reduces its own-fiber mass. Thus such an attaining cap passes through y even if this is implicit in the opening.

A zero-volume B threshold lies at or above support. Properness of the A cut makes the decrease strict when a threshold above support is lowered while the middle cut is fixed. The balanced circuit then covers K and A using the actual thresholds.

Fixed-normal equalization gives w≤2(Q−w). The ordered cover bound applies to both convex fibers with reversed ordering of Q−U_i, and summing gives a+k≤(Q+w)/Γ≤5Q/(3Γ). Under the bad target this gives Q≤3Γb and k≤3b.

After standardizing and recentering, barycentric vertex replacement bounds B by a translated cube of volume 2^d, and the nearest simplex face is at distance r. Thus L≤C_db, δL≤r and ω_{d−1}δL^d/b≤(1−2Γ)/2. These estimates check for all d≥2.
Matched the frozen source section locators to the original proofs and verified raw source hashes against the pinned graph.

dependencies.hypotheses: The actual three positive fibers satisfy midpoint compatibility. A depth-attaining cap with maximal A capture w has middle capture Q−w and B capture zero. Apply U+V≤2q.
The balanced cap families cover A and K and have nonzero continuous normals. Apply the top-three bound in dimension d≥2 with coefficients 1,1,1/Γ−2 to their respective ordered cap areas.

The two actual supporting B traces have unit transformed normals, all fibers and the common mark are retained by the affine map, and b≤a+k. The computed L, δL and missed mass satisfy the two explicit pair-lemma hypotheses. Same-wave predecessor approval required.
